buzzRounds.topic: Tarik Skubal reportedly picks the Mets in a record pitcher deal
buzzRounds.whatHappened: Two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the New York Mets over the weekend, according to multiple reports; the Mets haven't confirmed it because it's pending a physical. The Athletic reported Toronto had offered nine years and just over $400 million.
buzzRounds.whyCare: It would be the richest contract ever for a pitcher, passing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers, and only Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker and Juan Soto earn more per season.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Tarik Skubal has reportedly agreed to join the Mets for nine years and $450 million, the biggest contract a pitcher has ever signed, and he picked New York over a Blue Jays offer of just over $400 million.

details.name: Tarik Skubal
details.buzz: Skubal, a two-time Cy Young winner with Detroit, went 12-7 with a 2.72 earned run average in 2026, a season split between Detroit and the Dodgers, who traded for him on August 2.

buzzRounds.topic: One week to a likely lockout, and the sides are far apart
buzzRounds.whatHappened: Baseball's labor contract expires December 1 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern, and owners are expected to lock out the players, meaning no signings or trades until a new deal. In talks on Monday, November 23, owners again proposed a salary cap, a limit on what each team can spend on players, plus a $1 million minimum salary, and the players' union countered with equal sharing of all media money and no cap.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Commissioner Rob Manfred says owners will only agree to a deal with a salary cap, and a lockout would be the sport's 10th work stoppage since 1972. Talks resumed a day after Tarik Skubal agreed to his record deal with the Mets.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Baseball's labor deal runs out December 1 and a lockout is expected; owners want a salary cap with a $1 million minimum salary, and the players countered on Monday with no cap at all.

details.buzz: Skubal, a two-time Cy Young winner with Detroit, went 12-7 with a 2.72 earned run average in 2026, a season split between Detroit and the Dodgers, who traded for him on August 2.

buzzRounds.topic: Cubs land Trevor Rogers and Teruaki Sato in two days
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Cubs agreed to a five-year, $120 million deal with former Orioles lefty Trevor Rogers on Monday night, then a six-year, $120 million deal with Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato on Tuesday morning, according to sources; neither has been confirmed by the team yet.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Sato won the Triple Crown in Japan's Central League this year, meaning he led it in batting average (.306), home runs (39) and runs batted in (106), and the Cubs moved before a lockout that could freeze signings on December 1.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: The Cubs just spent big twice in two days: Trevor Rogers for five years, then Teruaki Sato, who won Japan's Triple Crown with 39 home runs and 106 runs batted in.

details.name: Trevor Rogers
details.buzz: Rogers, 29, went 10-11 with a 4.03 earned run average for Baltimore in 2026 and turned down the Orioles' qualifying offer before agreeing to five years with Chicago.
details.source: ESPN, Trevor Rogers and Cubs reach five-year deal (https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/50579432/sources-free-agent-trevor-rogers-cubs-reach-5-year-deal)

details.name: Teruaki Sato
details.buzz: Sato, 27, won the Triple Crown in Japan's Central League in 2026, leading it with a .306 average, 39 home runs and 106 runs batted in.

buzzRounds.topic: Mariners get Gold Glove third baseman Maikel Garcia
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Royals traded third baseman Maikel Garcia, reliever James McArthur and a minor-league pitcher to Seattle on November 18 for pitchers Bryce Miller, José A. Ferrer and Logan Evans, a six-player deal.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Garcia hit .286 with 16 home runs and won a Gold Glove in 2025, and ranks second among third basemen in Statcast fielding run value since 2023, filling a need for a Mariners team that finished 10 games under .500.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Seattle traded for Maikel Garcia, a Gold Glove third baseman who hit .286 in 2025, and sent pitcher Bryce Miller and two others to Kansas City in a six-player deal.

details.buzz: Garcia, a 2025 Gold Glove winner and All-Star, played only 82 games in 2026 because of hand and hamstring strains, hitting .268.

buzzRounds.topic: Silver Sluggers: Alonso, Caminero and Alvarez honored
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Silver Slugger Awards, given to the best hitter at each position in each league, were announced this past week, with 13 first-time winners. In the American League, Orioles first baseman Pete Alonso (43 home runs, 113 runs batted in), Rays third baseman Junior Caminero (42 home runs) and Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez (.316, 42 home runs) were among the winners.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Alvarez also won the American League Most Valuable Player award unanimously last week, and the Tigers had three winners: Dillon Dingler, Riley Greene and Rookie of the Year Kevin McGonigle.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Pete Alonso hit 43 home runs for Baltimore and just won a Silver Slugger, and so did Yordan Alvarez, who hit .316 with 42 homers and was a unanimous Most Valuable Player.

details.buzz: Alonso won the American League Silver Slugger at first base after hitting 43 home runs with 113 runs batted in, second most in the majors.
